what: Writing a per-query bound for the revision harness and restart_rows.py, the name of the column that holds a query's name in `query_counts` could not be taken from the debugging skill: its cycle example selects `kind`, while the view `counts_by_cause` (crates/blaze-profile/sql/examples.sql) selects `query`. The script was first written against `kind` and would have read every count as absent, which a write-only lane cannot see.
whys: The skill's SQL examples are prose in a markdown file; nothing runs them against the schema.
The schema's column names live in blaze-profile's writer, the views in a .sql file, the skill in a third place.
A lane that runs nothing has only the text to go by, so a stale example becomes code.
class: Documentation that quotes a schema without being checked against it.
prevention: The docs script (scripts/src/bin/docs.rs) extracts each SQL block of the debugging skill and the docs and prepares it against an empty database of the profile's schema, failing the gate on an unknown column; scripts read counts through `blaze explain <view> --json`, whose columns the view's test already fixes.
where: .claude/skills/debugging/SKILL.md ("SELECT kind, ran_cycle, executed FROM query_counts"); crates/blaze-profile/sql/examples.sql `counts_by_cause`
cause: Not confirmed which of the two is the table's column: the view was taken as the truth because it is compiled into blaze.
cost: one wrong draft, caught by reading the view
workaround: Read crates/blaze-profile/sql/examples.sql for a view's columns, never the skill's examples.
